newsitem.title: UK: Sterling firms vs dollar, little changed vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Sterling firms vs dollar, little changed vs mark.

text.p: Sterling settled below 59-month highs of 2.8665 marks set overnight, with traders looking for it to resume its climb in the days ahead amid expectations U.K. interest rates are poised to rise.
"We'll see a push up to 2.87 but the real target has got to be 2.90 now," said a trader on the Dublin floor of Finex, the financial products division of the New York Cotton Exchange.

Sterling was at 2.8620/30 at 1115 GMT from 2.8605/15 late Friday in Europe. Cable was at $1.6581/91 from $16548/53 Friday. Sterling's trade-weighted index, which has surged more than 19 percent since August 1996, was unchanged from Friday at 101.2.

The pound has gained more than one percent against the mark and the dollar since a report on Wednesday showed U.K. retail sales surged 1.1 percent in May, with the quarterly rate of increase the highest since July 1988.

"Growth in the U.K. looks as if it has stepped up a gear," said David Philpotts, the U.K. economist at Schroeder. "The economic numbers last week were all pretty strong and provided a pretty favourable backdrop for sterling."
While the underlying inflation rate hit the government's 2.5 percent target in April and May, analysts are looking for price rises to accelerate unless consumption is reined in.
This has stoked expectations that the Bank of England's new monetary policy committee will raise interest rates from 6.5 percent at its next meeting on July 10.
September short sterling was down six basis points at 92.98, implying official interest rates of more than 7 percent by the end of the third quarter of 1997.

A communique issued by the Group of Seven leading industrial nations after their weekend summit also hinted at the risks to inflation, saying Britain needs to keep inflation in check and cut its budget deficit further.
